finding.title: Extract repeated MaterialApp/ProviderScope pump boilerplate in bulk_mark_screen_test.dart and empty_login_ws2_test.dart
finding.why: No shared pumpApp test helper exists anywhere in the repo (a grep of test/helpers/ finds none), so TQ-3 has nothing to point tests at yet. bulk_mark_screen_test.dart hand-rolls the identical ProviderScope+MaterialApp+localizationsDelegates block 5 times in one file. empty_login_ws2_test.dart duplicates it 2 more times even though the same file already defines a _wrapWithProviders helper that isn't reused for those 2 tests. Every AppLocalizations delegate or supported-locale change has to be hand-edited at each duplicate site.
finding.recommendation: Add a shared test/helpers/pump_app.dart with a pumpApp(tester, child, {overrides, locale}) helper; migrate bulk_mark_screen_test.dart's 5 sites onto it and repoint empty_login_ws2_test.dart's 2 stray sites onto the file's own _wrapWithProviders.
acceptance_criteria: bulk_mark_screen_test.dart contains a single MaterialApp construction (via a helper), not 5
empty_login_ws2_test.dart's 2 profile-creation tests use _wrapWithProviders like the rest of the file

finding.title: Fix onboarding_screen_l1_test.dart's intentChooser Hebrew assertion to match the real ARB string
finding.why: The test's Hebrew string (present-tense 'מביא') does not match the real onboardingIntentHeading ARB value (past-tense 'הביא') — one word differs. Because the assertion checks findsNothing for a string that was never going to be found either way, it passes unconditionally and verifies nothing, even though the test's own docstring states the suite's purpose is guarding against English-string leaks into the Hebrew locale for this exact screen.
finding.recommendation: Load the real string via AppLocalizations.delegate.load(Locale('he')) — as app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart already does for its own Hebrew assertions — and assert find.text(he.onboardingIntentHeading) findsOneWidget.
acceptance_criteria: Temporarily reverting onboardingIntentHeading's Hebrew ARB value to the English literal makes this test fail

finding.title: Type the catch clause in CurriculumImportService._activateOne so Error subtypes aren't swallowed as activation failures
finding.why: A bare `catch (e)` also catches Error subtypes (StateError, TypeError, a failed assertion). A genuine programming bug during activation is silently reported to the onboarding UI as an ordinary 'this curriculum failed to activate' result instead of surfacing as a crash, masking the real defect behind a plausible-looking user-facing failure. (This bare-catch pattern recurs ~54 times repo-wide; only this batch's site is counted here.)
finding.recommendation: Narrow to `on Exception catch (e)` (or the specific exception types _activationService.activate can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate.
acceptance_criteria: A test that makes the mocked activationService throw a StateError confirms it propagates out of _activateOne/importSingle instead of becoming a CurriculumImportResult(success: false)

finding.title: Extract the hardcoded 'לימוד' stage-name sentinel to a shared constant
finding.why: DomainTermLabels.resolveStoredStageName documents this literal as the canonical sentinel matched via HebrewTerms.stageNameMap to resolve the correct localized stage name at render time — it is load-bearing, not decorative. It's independently hand-typed in 3 separate files (2 sites in this batch's paired lib file) with no shared constant tying them together; a typo in one copy would silently break resolveStoredStageName's lookup for stages created by that one code path only, and nothing would catch it since the value is a plain string, not a shared symbol.
finding.recommendation: Add a single `const kLimudStageName = 'לימוד';` (near HebrewTerms.stageNameMap or in core/constants) and reference it from all 3 write sites instead of retyping the literal.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "stageName: 'לימוד'" lib/ returns only the shared constant's own definition, not literal duplicates at the 3 call sites

finding.title: Confirm whether Positioned(left:/right:) illustration badges in intro pages need PositionedDirectional for RTL
finding.why: AX-1's RTL rule is written against EdgeInsets.only(left/right) and Alignment.centerLeft/Right, but Positioned(left:/right:) has the identical non-mirroring failure mode under RTL that PositionedDirectional(start:/end:) avoids. app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's RTL smoke test only checks the screen mounts without throwing, not badge placement, so a mirroring regression on these floating badges in Hebrew locale would not be caught. This may be an intentional 'decorative collage doesn't need to mirror' choice rather than a bug — needs a visual check to confirm either way.
finding.recommendation: Take a Locale('he') screenshot of AppIntroScreen pages 2-3 (reusing the app_intro_rewards_cta_overlap_test.dart rig) and confirm badge placement reads correctly; switch to PositionedDirectional(start:/end:) if not.
acceptance_criteria: A golden or screenshot test of pages 2-3 in Locale('he') exists and has been reviewed for correct badge placement
